key_insight: CsPbBr3 contains a hierarchical herringbone network of polar domain walls—ferroelastic twin walls and antiphase walls—whose local inversion symmetry is broken despite the bulk crystal being non-polar.
engineering_relevance: These polar nano-walls could alter carrier transport and polarization in halide perovskite devices, making domain-wall engineering a potential lever for optoelectronic performance.
method: Atomic-scale imaging to resolve wall structure and symmetry
In-situ heating to track wall formation during phase transitions
Comparison of twin walls and antiphase walls in the same lattice
evidence_signal: The abstract reports atomic-resolution structural imaging plus in-situ thermal experiments showing the two wall types form sequentially during symmetry-lowering phase transitions.
watch_item: The transport impact is suggested but not directly quantified, so device-level benefits remain to be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Revealing Polar Walls in CsPbBr3: Herringbone Structure and Formation Pathway
